newsitem.title: PERU: Japanese Foreign Minister arrives in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Japanese Foreign Minister arrives in Peru.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda arrived in Lima early on Thursday to hear firsthand how Peru's military ended the 18-week-long hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence.

Ikeda, who travelled with family members of the two dozen Japanese diplomats and businessmen among 71 hostages rescued in Tuesday's daring assault, was met by Peruvian Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi at Lima's military airport on his arrival soon after midnight local time (0500 GMT).
The Japanese delegation of Foreign Ministry and military officials, businessmen, relatives and journalists numbered about 120 people, local radio reported.
During his stay in Lima, Ikeda was also due to supervise the re-opening of the Japanese Embassy in Lima.

One Peruvian judge hostage, two soldiers and all 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels were killed in Tuesday's assault, which was ordered without Japn's knowledge by Peru's President Alberto Fujimori.
